chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Manquri, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) who said:

I hope for the salvation of this nation for whoever recognizes our right among them, except for one of three: the companion of the unjust ruler, the companion of selfish desire, and the openly corrupt sinner.

key_terms.حَقَّنَا: Our right (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Who are the three exceptions to those who will be saved according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) identifying three specific archetypes—oppressive rulers, those driven by base desires, and openly sinful individuals—who are excluded from the general hope of salvation for the Ummah. This hadith highlights the Shia theological emphasis on *Wilayah* (recognition of the Ahl al-Bayt's right) as the primary criterion for communal salvation, while distinguishing between those who recognize it but fail in practice due to tyranny, ego, or open transgression.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-107 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Minqari, on the authority of Hafs ibn Qiyath al-Nakha’ee that Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“Anyone in this nation who has recognized our right can hope to be saved but three: one who helps the oppressive King; one who follows his selfish desires; and one who engages in corrupt deeds in public.”
